about: Gate for run_browser_tests.py. Every browser-groups.json entry runs and must pass, except those named here. Adding a name here changes what the gate accepts: docs/hars/BROWSER-TESTS.md lists every entry and the runner prints them in its summary.

replay_layout.reason: HARS serves its own pre-release version (v2.0.0-alpha.4) in the version label; line 214 requires ^v[0-9]+[.][0-9]+[.][0-9]+$. Intended difference while HARS is a pre-release.
replay_layout.message: version is an info line in ⋯

video_overlay.reason: Line 77 reads document.activeElement right after the dialog is hidden, but the app hands focus on from the dialog's close event (video-overlay.js), which arrives a few ms later; read before it, focus is still on the hidden 초기화 button. Same with the Python server. Not a HARS difference; the behaviour itself is checked by guarded_by on every run.
video_overlay.remove_when: the upstream test is fixed and imported again

video_overlay[hars_focus_check].reason: What video_overlay.cjs line 77 guards (Escape closes 겹쳐 보기 설정 and focus belongs to nothing), with the dialog's close event awaited before the same condition. Runs whenever video_overlay runs and must pass.

replay_format2.reason: Imports the Python converter's compact.py (compact_data, expand_frames) to build replay format 2 and compares app.js's expansion with it. HARS has no Python converter; the test uses neither the server nor the HARS pages.
replay_format2.replaced_by: Encoder side: integration/pipeline_contract.py (CI, synthetic input) and integration/real_conversion_compare.py (13/14/47 real segments, local) require HARS's whole replayV2 output to equal the Python converter's; scripts/verify_reference.py keeps app.js as preserved. Gap: nothing in HARS runs app.js's format 2 expansion on HARS output; that rests on the upstream test having passed against the Python output HARS equals.
